quiz.q: Where on the résumé should relevant certifications go?
options: At the very end, after the declaration
At the top, so the recruiter sees them immediately
quiz.explain: Recruiters have no time to search; a certification at the top puts you ahead of uncertified candidates only if it's seen.

quiz.q: Why does the sample profile summary use both "Mule ESB developer" and "MuleSoft developer"?
options: Job sites like Naukri and LinkedIn search with both keywords
Mule ESB is the newer name
quiz.explain: Both keywords are used by job sites, so use both across the résumé — and vary forms like web services / REST APIs / RESTful API.

quiz.q: In the technical skills table, why is RAML listed under ESB skills rather than programming skills?
options: RAML is a modeling language, not a programming language
RAML only runs on Mule ESB
Recruiters don't read the programming row
quiz.explain: RAML (RESTful API Modeling Language) describes APIs; DataWeave is the programming skill.

quiz.q: What makes an Achievements point effective, according to the class?
options: Quantified results (e.g. a 40% reduction) that you can explain in detail
quiz.explain: Numbers give a better impression, and you must have the explanation ready — never keep a point you can't explain.

quiz.q: You haven't built CI/CD pipelines yourself, only used them. What is the suggested answer to "Have you created a pipeline?"
options: Say yes and describe Jenkins in general
Say you used it and debugged failures, a separate DevOps team built it, and you're ready to learn
Say CI/CD isn't used in MuleSoft
quiz.explain: Answer honestly; creating pipelines is an added advantage, and you shouldn't claim what you can't answer questions on.

quiz.q: What is the main difference between an API and a web service, as defined in class?
options: APIs use XML; web services use JSON
A web service is code that lets systems communicate and exchange data over the internet; an API need not use the internet
quiz.explain: An API helps systems communicate and exchange data; a web service does so over the internet, and comes in REST and SOAP types.

quiz.q: Which statement about SOAP is correct?
options: It accepts JSON, XML, HTML and text
It is an XML-based protocol documented with WSDL and defines its own security
It inherits security from the transport layer
quiz.explain: SOAP (Simple Object Access Protocol) is XML-only, uses WSDL, and defines its own security; REST inherits it from the transport.

quiz.q: A requirement needs response caching. Which style should you choose?
quiz.explain: SOAP doesn't support caching; choose REST whenever caching is required. SOAP suits strong security and standardized communication.

quiz.q: You need all active accounts of a bank (`/accounts?status=active`). Which parameter type is this?
quiz.explain: Query parameters filter, sort and paginate a collection, after `?`. URI parameters like `/{customerId}` identify one unique resource.

quiz.q: A resource may or may not exist; you want to update it completely if it does, or create it if it doesn't. Which method?
quiz.explain: PUT fully updates or creates; POST creates a new resource; PATCH partially updates.

quiz.q: A consumer creates a customer with a customer ID that already exists. Which status code fits?
quiz.explain: 409 means the request conflicts with the current state of the resource — e.g. a duplicate.

quiz.q: A consumer exceeds the limit set by the Rate Limiting policy. What status code do they get?
quiz.explain: 429 Too Many Requests — the client exceeded the number of requests allowed in a period.

quiz.q: The consumer has access to one resource but calls another it isn't allowed to use. Which code?
quiz.explain: 403: the server understood the request but the user isn't allowed. 401 is for missing/invalid credentials.

quiz.q: You send XML to an endpoint that only accepts JSON. Which code is expected?
quiz.explain: 415 Unsupported Media Type — e.g. XML or CSV sent instead of JSON.

quiz.q: Running locally with Autodiscovery enabled, every request returns 503. What fixes it?
options: Disable the Anypoint Platform gatekeeper property or comment out the Autodiscovery ID
quiz.explain: 503 Service Unavailable appears locally when Autodiscovery is enabled without the gatekeeper disabled.

cards.front: What decides whether you get an interview call?
cards.back: The résumé and Naukri profile get you the call; your confidence on the recruiter call decides whether the interview is scheduled.

cards.front: Three things the profile summary should cover
cards.back: Total and relevant experience, technical expertise, and soft skills (communication, teamwork).

cards.front: Why name every Anypoint component in the summary?
cards.back: So the profile is shortlisted if the job description mentions any of them (Studio, Design Center, Exchange, API Manager, Runtime Manager, Anypoint Monitoring).

cards.front: Rule for listing connectors, components, policies and tools
cards.back: Only list what you can answer — at least 50–60% knowledge. Each item steers the interview towards it.
JMS ≈ VM; File ≈ FTP ≈ SFTP — learn one and you can handle the other.

cards.front: Asked about a connector you haven't used?
cards.back: If you know it, say you did a POC but haven't used it in real time; if you don't, say so plainly.

cards.front: Why is MuleSoft listed under "ESB skills"?
cards.back: It's an Enterprise Service Bus — it facilitates orchestration, transformation and enrichment.
Client, Duration (matching your experience dates), Domain, Role, Environments (e.g. DR for banking), Team size; optionally connectors used.

cards.front: Why include DR in a banking project's environments?
cards.back: Disaster Recovery is critical for banking and finance; explaining it well can tip the decision.
5–6, written in different words for each project — don't copy-paste. Include at least two MuleSoft projects.
1) Interest in the role with total and MuleSoft experience, 2) technical skills, 3) non-technical skills, 4) résumé attached and closing. Personalise the recruiter's name; clear subject line.
Tell me about yourself; explain your project; explain your current roles and responsibilities. They steer the interviewer along your path.

cards.front: What must "tell me about yourself" cover?
cards.back: Total experience → relevant experience → achievements/certifications → projects and domains → then "Coming to the recent project…". About 2–5 minutes.
In MuleSoft a single API or application is also called a "project".

Jira story → docs/queries → RAML in Design Center + feedback → import to Studio and implement → MUnit 80% → peer & architect review → Dev → SIT → UAT → performance test → Prod → hypercare → KT → Confluence.
The initial support period after go-live (15–30 days depending on the organization).
Greet by the **interviewer's** time of day (good morning/afternoon/evening) — never "good night".
Application Programming Interface — code that helps two or more systems communicate and exchange data.
Code that helps systems communicate and exchange data **over the internet**. Two types: REST and SOAP.

cards.front: What is a REST web service?
cards.back: Representational State Transfer — follows HTTP, accepts JSON, XML, HTML and text/plain, documented with RAML in Design Center.

cards.front: What is a SOAP web service?
cards.back: Simple Object Access Protocol — XML-based, XML input only, documented with WSDL, platform- and language-independent.
SOAP is a protocol, WSDL, XML only, more bandwidth, own security, no caching. REST is an architectural pattern, RAML, many formats, lighter, inherits transport security, caching possible.

cards.front: When to choose REST vs. SOAP?
cards.back: REST for simplicity, flexibility and whenever caching is needed. SOAP for complex, highly secure, standardized communication.
Query params filter/sort/paginate, after `?` (`/accounts?status=active`). URI params identify one unique resource, in the path (`/{customerId}`).
GET (fetch, 200), POST (create, 201), PUT (full update or create), PATCH (partial update), DELETE.
POST creates a new resource; PUT updates completely if it exists or creates it; PATCH updates partially.
1xx informational, 2xx success, 3xx redirection, 4xx client error, 5xx server error.
200 OK with data; 201 Created (response to POST); 204 success with no content.
400 bad/undesired format or missing params; 401 missing/wrong credentials; 403 understood but not allowed.
E.g. a GET sent to a POST-only resource.
409 Conflict (duplicate), 415 Unsupported Media Type (XML instead of JSON), 429 Too Many Requests (rate limit exceeded).
500: server hit an error (e.g. DB down). 501: server doesn't support the functionality.
502 Bad Gateway: the gateway got no response from upstream. 504 Gateway Timeout: no timely response (e.g. slower than the gateway's 300 ms).
The app is down/not running — also seen locally with Autodiscovery enabled unless the gatekeeper is disabled.
RESTful API Modeling Language — a YAML-based language to describe REST APIs: requests, responses, schemas, examples, resources, methods, security schemes.

cards.front: What is a trait in RAML?
cards.back: A reusable component, similar to a function, declaring common properties for HTTP methods.
